lessonPlan.topic: Student Book P.17 Audio: track 27 - A Listen. Then act it out.

details: This activity checks understanding of language and vocabulary in a story using visuals as an aid.
Look for careful listening of the story, then confident repetition of story sentences.
“ I really want chicken today, but there’s no chicken left in the cafeteria! Let’s listen to this story about Tim and Amy — maybe they had the same problem.”

Heads Up (Reading): 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and help Ss to understand the text by asking questions, practicing skimming (reading for gist), scanning (reading for specific information) and detail (reading for comprehension). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down (Listen and Follow): 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together (Video, then act it out): 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book P.17 Audio: track 27 - B. Look and choose

details: Look and choose tests students’ understanding of story using picture and word based MC questions.
Look for correct answers  and neat circling in students’ books.
“I don’t really want pizza either. I’m feeling sad.  What can I do now?”

Heads Down:

Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.71 - A Read and number

details: Read and number checks students’ understanding of a similar story by reading short dialogues and ordering the pictures.
Look for correct numbering and neat writing of numbers.
“I’m so hungry I’m starting to think maybe I should eat the pizza after all. Let’s read this new story and put the pictures in order — maybe it will help me decide.”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.50 - C Make your own story

details: Make your own story gives students the opportunity to personalise a story by circling words or stickers. Then they practise speaking by telling the story.
Look for accurate word choices and sticker placement inside the story pictures and confident story telling.
“I’m even hungrier now! I finally decided to ask for pizza… but they don’t have any left! Let’s make our own stories and see what these children ask for.”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.50 - Tongue Twisters Listen and say Audio: track 28

details: Listen and say practises the pronunciation of words with /s/ and /z/ at sentence level.
Look for clear pronunciation of words in the sentences and confident repetition.

“Well, school is almost finished, and I didn’t get my favourite food today. But it’s okay — I can ask my mum and dad to make something delicious tonight. Let’s celebrate with some tongue twisters before we go!”
